cards.explanation: The answer is the food offerings to the LORD. Moses says the priests "…are to eat the food offerings to the LORD; that is their inheritance." (Deuteronomy 18:1) The whole tribe of Levi has no portion or inheritance with Israel, so those offerings are what Moses names as theirs. That's a different kind of inheritance than the rest of Israel gets.

The answer is LORD. Moses says, "…the LORD is their inheritance, as He promised them." (Deuteronomy 18:2) The Levites have no inheritance among their brothers, but they have Him. And Moses says He is the One who promised it. The LORD Himself is what they get.

The answer is chosen. Moses says, "…the LORD your God has chosen Levi and his sons out of all your tribes to stand and minister in His name for all time." (Deuteronomy 18:5) So the gifts go with the job: standing and ministering in His name. And "…for all time." is no short-term contract, friends.

The answer is True. Moses says the Levite "…shall eat equal portions, even though he has received money from the sale of his father’s estate." (Deuteronomy 18:8) So his side money doesn't shrink his share. Everybody at that table gets the same portion.

The answer is consulting a medium. Moses lists someone who "…consults a medium or spiritist, or inquires of the dead." (Deuteronomy 18:11) Those belong on the list of things Israel was not to do. It's a serious list, so we just keep it plain.

The answer is because of their detestable practices. Moses says, "…because of these detestable things, the LORD your God is driving out the nations before you." (Deuteronomy 18:12) Just before that, he lists the things, like divination, sorcery and consulting a medium (Deuteronomy 18:10, 11). So the reason is the practices themselves, and Moses names them plainly.

The answer is False. Moses says, "Though these nations, which you will dispossess, listen to conjurers and diviners, the LORD your God has not permitted you to do so." (Deuteronomy 18:14) The nations may do it, but Israel is not allowed to.

The answer is from among Israel's own people. Moses says, "The LORD your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your brothers. You must listen to him." (Deuteronomy 18:15) This prophet comes from among their own brothers. The people already know where to look, friends.

The answer is not to hear His voice anymore. The people said, "Let us not hear the voice of the LORD our God or see this great fire anymore, so that we will not die!" (Deuteronomy 18:16) I think that voice and that fire were more than they could stand. I bet my mustache would have stood straight up.
The answer is False. The LORD told Moses, "They have spoken well." (Deuteronomy 18:17) Moses doesn't say He was angry. Then the LORD goes on to promise a prophet (Deuteronomy 18:18).

The answer is words. The LORD says, "I will put My words in his mouth, and he will tell them everything I command him." (Deuteronomy 18:18) The prophet carries God's words, not his own. That's a pretty big job, friends.

The answer is True. The LORD says, "…if any prophet dares to speak a message in My name that I have not commanded him to speak, or to speak in the name of other gods, that prophet must be put to death." (Deuteronomy 18:20) It's a heavy verse, and I think it shows how seriously God takes His words. Two things are named here: speaking in His name what He didn't command, and speaking in the name of other gods.

The answer is it never comes true. Moses says, "When a prophet speaks in the name of the LORD and the message does not come to pass or come true, that is a message the LORD has not spoken." (Deuteronomy 18:22) So a message that never comes true is one the LORD has not spoken. Then Moses adds that the prophet has spoken presumptuously, and tells the people, "Do not be afraid of him."

The answer is False. When the message doesn't come true, Moses says, "The prophet has spoken presumptuously. Do not be afraid of him." (Deuteronomy 18:22) No fear needed, friends. I wish somebody had told that to me about the vacuum cleaner.
